posts.cooked:
Wow, this escalated a bit more than I was expecting. Here’s the big reason for me asking the questions and the answer about Claude is on my radar. I started using Super Grok to help me troubleshoot IT issues at work. It’s true that AI skims data in an attempt to summarize what you’re asking for it. Super Grok would give 4 agents that would essentially “debate” the answer they’d give before giving it. What I found is it was really good at digging deep in to factual data with number based backup, and that gave cool approximations of how much DPS a talent node would add, or theoreticals on how moving to one secondary stat might pay off in spite of guides saying otherwise. It was helpful. They’ve now paywalled that part to a crazy price and the normal Super Grok barely feels better than ChatGPT which I’m pretty annoyed about, especially after going for the yearly option.

In relation to WoW Arena Logs, it’s not the data isn’t open to the public, it’s that they use a specific type of code to store and display the data and AI can’t scrape it by going to the URLs. So you have to download multiple CSVs, then AI can congregate them, give you averages, etc. I do wish WoW Arena Logs could database the info better because it could give some great realistic info on talent and stat choices and how the damage works over broad averages.

AI is both over and under marketed way too much. I think the whole, whatever nation wins in AI will rule the world stuff is going to age like milk. At it’s core, yes, it’s a data scraper. But the idea that it just grabs opinions from forums and it’s answers are borderline worthless is inaccurate as well. Take the CSV thing for example, any person with Excel knowledge can do the same thing as what AI is doing, but it will take a lot of manual copy paste time. AI can do all the heavy lifting and provide really great numbers in a matter of a minute or less. That’s where it shines as a tool.

AI shouldn’t replace analysts because it’s really bad at making decisions, but analysts will be able to make much stronger decisions more efficiently because AI can grab and consolidate levels of data that a single person would only dream of being able to do before. Seems like Claude is a strong potential contender for better data so those replies help.
